full_judgment: 33. Order XXXIX, rules 1 and 2 monitors grant of temporary injunction. Order XXXIX, rule 1 controls temporary injunction in respect of any property in dispute in a suit which is in danger of being wasted, damaged or alienated by any party to the suit, or wrongfully sold in execution of decree, or that the defendant threatens, or intends, to remove or dispose of his property with a view to defraud his creditors. Order XXXIX, rule 1 is not relevant for our purpose. Order XXXIX rule 2 is relevant for the purpose. Rule 2 regulates the grant of temporary injunction against apprehended breach of contract or other injury of any kind arising out of the same contract or relating to the same property or legal right. There is no scope for extending the provision in any respect by inference or analogy. The terms of provisions of Order XXXIX, rules 1 and 2 do not appear to expressly authorise the exercise of power of granting interlocutory injunction in mandatory shape under the provisions of Order XXXIX, rules 1 and 2. The Court, of course, in the exercise of inherent power under section 151 has got jurisdiction to issue direction in mandatory form or to grant interlocutory mandatory injunction.
